1. This appeal has been filed by the appellant - State under Section 378(1)(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Code') against the order passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Himmatnagar (hereinafter referred to as 'the learned Trial Court') in Criminal Case No. 2231 of 2007 on 23.03.2011, whereby, the learned Trial NEUTRAL CITATION State Of Gujarat - Thro' D C Patel vs Dayaldas Gordhandas Hotvani Vendor And ... on 20 August, 2025

1 R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined Court has acquitted the respondent - accused from the offences punishable under Section 7(1)(2)(5) and Rules 32 and 62 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').
1.1. The respondent is hereinafter referred to as 'the accused' as he stood in the rank and file in the original case, for the sake of convenience, clarity and brevity.

2. The relevant facts leading to filing of the present appeal are as under:
2.1.

On 08.06.2006, at around 9:30am, the complainant, Dilipkumar Chandrakantbhai Patel, Food Inspector, went to M/s.
Dayaldas Gordhandas Hotwani's shop, situated in Old Bazaar, Opposite the Dargah, at Himmatnagar, District Sabarkantha, and after the due procedure, took a packed sample of 'Manikchand Gutkha'.

The entire procedure was done, and the sample was sent to the Public Analyst, and as per the report of the Public Aanalyst, the sample of 'Manikchand Gutkha' was adulterated, and did not comply with Rule-62 and was misbranded under Rule-32(B) of the Prevention Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

The NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined complaint was filed before the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sabarkantha at Himmatnagar, which came to be registered as Criminal Case No. 2231 of 2007. 2.2.

sentences.text: The accused was duly served with the summons and the accused appeared before the learned Trial Court and it was verified whether the copies of all the papers were provided to the accused as per the provisions of Section 207 of the Code.
As the case was a private warrant triable case, the evidence of the complainant on oath was recorded and the complainant has produced 33 documentary evidence in support of his case.

Considering the evidence on record, as a prima-facie case was made out, a charge was framed by the learned Trial Court at Exh.11 and the statement of the accused was recorded at Exh.12, wherein, the accused denied all the contents of the charge and the further evidence of the prosecution was taken on record.

The prosecution examined 2 witnesses i.e. the complainant - D.C.Patel, Food Inspector at Exh.18 and PW-2 Hanumantrao Marutirao Rakshi at Exh.56 and has produced documentary evidences in support of the case.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined 2.3
After the evidence of the complainant was closed, the further statement of the accused under Section 313 of the Code was recorded wherein in the accused denied the evidence on record.

After hearing the arguments of the learned APP and learned advocate for the accused and after perusing the documents on record, the learned Trial Court, by the impugned judgment and order, was pleased to acquit the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 7(1)(2)(5) and Rules - 32 and 62 of the Act.

3. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Trial Court, the appellant - State has filed the present appeal mainly stating that the impugned judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court is contrary to law, evidences on record and principles of natural justice.

The learned Trial Court has erred in evaluating the evidence on record of the case and without appreciating the evidence in its real perspective, acquitted the State Of Gujarat - Thro' D C Patel vs Dayaldas Gordhandas Hotvani Vendor And ... on 20 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118692209/
2 accused.

There are direct and indirect evidence connecting the respondent with the crime which are produced in the Court and in spite of this fact, the learned Trial Court, without appreciating NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined oral as well as documentary evidence on record of the case, straight way has arrived at a conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.

The learned Trial Court has erred in not considering the ratio laid down by the judgment of the Apex Court which are applicable to the facts of the present case and the impugned judgment and order is perverse and suffering from legal and factual error apparent on the record.
The learned Trial Court has erred in not considering the evidence of the complainant and other witnesses which was fully supported the case of the prosecution.

The learned Trial Court has passed the impugned judgment and order of acquittal without giving any cogent and convincing reasons and the same is illegal, invalid and improper, and therefore, the same requires to be quashed and set aside.
4. Heard learned APP Ms.C.M.Shah for the appellant - State and learned advocate Mr. Deep Brahmbhatt for the respondent no. 1 - accused.
Perused the impugned judgment and order of acquittal and have re-appreciated the entire evidence of the prosecution on record of the case.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined 5.

Learned APP Ms.C.M.Shah for the appellant - State has taken this Court through the entire evidence produced by the prosecution and has vehemently argued that the learned Trial Court has not appreciated the evidence properly and the prosecution has produced cogent evidence to prove the case and has successfully proved the case against the accused but the learned Trial Court has not considered the same and has acquitted the accused.
The judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Judge is contrary to law, evidence on record and principles of justice.
The judgment and order of acquittal passed by learned Judge is based on inferences, not warranted by facts of the case and also on presumptions, not permitted by law.
Learned APP has urged this Court to quash and set aside the impugned judgment and order of acquittal and to find the accused guilty for the said offence and impose maximum sentence on the accused.

6. Learned advocate Mr.Deep Brahmbhatt for the respondent has submitted that the learned Trial Court has appreciated all the evidence in true perspective and has not committed any error in acquitting the accused.

Therefore, no NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined interference of this Court is required in the impugned judgment and the order of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court and has urged this Court to reject the appeal.

7. It is a settled principle of law that in an appeal against acquittal, the Appellate Court is circumscribed by limitation that no interference has to be made in the order of acquittal unless after appreciation of the evidence produced before the learned Trial Court, it appears that there are some manifest illegality or perversity which could not have been possibly arrived at by the Court.

It is also a settled principle that there is no embargo on the Appellate Court to review the evidence but,
generally the order of acquittal shall not be interfered with as the presumption of innocence of the accused is further strengthened by the order of acquittal.

web of administration of justice in criminal cases is that if two views are possible on the evidence adduced in the case of the prosecution i.e. (i) guilt of the accused and (ii) his innocence, the view,
which is in favour of the accused, should be adopted, and

if the trial Court has taken the view in favour of the accused, the Appellate Court should NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined not disturb the findings of the acquittal.

The Appellate Court can interfere with the judgment and order of acquittal only when there are compelling and substantial reasons and the order is clearly unreasonable and where the Appellate Court comes to conclusion that based on the evidence, the conviction is a must.
8.

In light of the above, the evidence produced by the prosecution on record is appreciated and PW-1, Dilipkumar Chandrakantbhai Patel, examined at Exh.18, is the complainant and Food Inspector, who has narrated in detail the entire procedure undertaken by him at the time of taking of the sample.

The complainant has produced his certificate of the Food Inspector's Training Class at Exh.19, a copy of the gazette at Exh.20, the intimation regarding taking of the sample at Exh.21,
receipt of Rs.75/- at Exh.22, receipt on the letter head of the accused at Exh.23, sample seal of the label at Exh.24, statement of witness Hanumantrao Marutiram Rakshi at Exh.25, the registration certificate of the shop of the accused at Exh.26, the statement of the accused at Exh.27, Form-7, by which, memorandum of the sample sent to the Public Analyst at Exh.28, parcel receipt at Exh.29,
letter sent to the Public Analyst at NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED:
20/08/2025 undefined Exh.30, R.P.A.D. Acknowledgement at Exh.31, letter sent to the Public Analyst regarding the sending of the sample by S.T.parcel at Exh.32, receipt of the Public Analyst at Exh.33, letter, by which, the remaining two samples were sent to the Local Health Authority at Exh.34, letter to the producer of the 'Manikchand Gutka' at Exh.35, envelope, which has returned unserved with the endorsement, refused by the producer of the 'Manikchand Gutka' at Exh.36,
sanction of the letter of the Local Health Authority at Exh.37, report of the Public Analyst at Exh.38,
letter to the producer for the information of the firm at Exh.39, envelope that has returned unserved at Exh.40, the registered post acknowledgement along with the registered post acknowledgement,
the letter to the accused to produce the bill at Exh.41, the postal acknowledgement of the letter sent to the accused at Exh.42, a letter requesting the details of the constitution of the firm sent to the producer at Exh.43, envelope addressed to the producer returned unserved with the endorsement 'refused' by the producer at Exh.44, letter seeking permission to file the case addressed to the Local Health Authority at Exh.45, permission given by the Local Health NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined Authority at Exh.46 and the order at Exh.47, the intimation given to the Local Health Authority that the case has been filed at Exh.48,
the intimation given to the accused by the Local Health Authority at Exh.49, and the yadi of the Local Health Authority at Exh.50.

During the cross- examination by the learned advocate for the accused, the complainant has admitted that in Appendix- B of the P.H.Act of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, there is no standard for gutka, and the sample that was taken was a packed sample.
The name and address was mentioned on the gutka pouch, and the registration number of the company was also mentioned on the pouch.
The expiry term of the gutka was six months and it was to be used within six months.
The manufacturer was not made a party to the proceeding and no permission was sought for to file a complaint against the manufacturer company.
Each pouch had the weight of two grams mentioned on it and the envelope at Exh.36 was sent to the producer company, which had returned unserved with the endorsement refused.

8.1. PW-2, Hanumantrao Marutiram Rakshi is the panch NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined witness of the panchnama, which is produced at Exh.25, but the witness has not supported the case of the prosecution and has not admitted that the sample was taken in his presence by the Food Inspector.

9. On appreciation of the entire evidence of the prosecution, from the evidence it has emerged that the sample was taken by the Food Inspector on 08.06.2006 and the complaint was filed on 07.07.2007 after a gap of more than one year and five months.
On the pouches of the gutka, the name of the manufacturer was mentioned and the accused was the vendor, but the manufacturer has not been joined as a party to the proceedings.

The Food Inspector did not seek permission for filing the case against the manufacturer and the Food Inspector had sought for the details of the manufacturing company by a letter, but the letter was refused.

Moreover, in the entire evidence,
there is no evidence to suggest that after the report of analysis of the Public Analyst was received by the Food Inspector, the procedure under section-13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was followed and the accused did not get a chance to exercise his statutory right for NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined getting the sample analyszed by the Central Food Laboratory.

There is no evidence on record that the report of the Public Analyst was sent to the accused informing him that if he so desired, he may make an application to the Court within a period of 10 days from the receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of 'Malikchand Gutka' analyzed by the Central Food Laboratory.
The Learned Trial Court has discussed the breach of the mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the PFA Act.

10. In view of the above, the learned trial Court has appreciated the entire evidence in proper perspective and there does not appear to be any infirmity and illegality in the impugned judgment and order of acquittal.

The learned Trial Court has appreciated all the evidence and this Court is of the considered opinion that the learned Trial Court was completely justified in acquitting the accused of the charges leveled against them.

The findings recorded by the learned Trial Court are absolutely just and proper and no illegality or infirmity has been committed by the learned trial Court and this Court is in complete agreement with the findings, ultimate conclusion and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1484/2011 JUDGMENT DATED: 20/08/2025 undefined the resultant order of acquittal recorded by the learned Trial Court.
This Court finds no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order and the present appeal is devoid of merits and resultantly, the same is dismissed.
11. The impugned order passed in Criminal Case No.2231 of 2007 by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Himmatnagar on 23.03.2011 is hereby confirmed.
12. Bail bond stands cancelled.
Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Trial Court forthwith.
